newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle futures end sharply lower.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures ended sharply lower on a surge to higher levels in corn futures, traders said. Live cattle futures were also influenced by corn values which combined with profit taking and position rolling to knock nearby month lower at the close while deferreds ended up.
Feeder cattle closed 1.150 to 0.500 cent per lb lower with March off 0.625 at 68.325 cents. Live cattle ended 0.375 cent lower to 0.175 higher with April off most at 69.250 cents.
Sources noted that higher feed costs, as indicated by higher corn futures, would cut demand for replacement feeders, traders said.
"It was a grain story today" that accounted for the bulk of selling in feeder cattle, said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc.
The CME feeder cattle index rose $0.06 to $69.11 per cwt.

E.D.& F. Man and Prudential Securities sold active May much of the day and Cargill Investor Services sold late, traders said. LIT division of First Options spread long May/short March before E.D.&F. Man bought March. Cargill spread long August feeders/ short December live cattle after spreading long November feeders/short April live cattle early.
Higher grain futures supported deferred live cattle. Rising feed costs could cut cattle placements on feed and result in fewer fed cattle and beef later, traders said.

Nearby live cattle drifted back from early losses around midsession, underpinned by traders that still expect further strength in cash cattle markets. However, prices retreated again when cash beef prices showed the first slippage in two weeks, they said.
The price for heavy-weight choice boxed beef rose Friday to $107.25 per cwt, a $7.85 gain for the week and the highest level since December 30. But prices were mostly lower at midday Monday.

The premium of futures to cash, profit taking and rolling of longs into back months also weighed on April late and that month ended near its days lows. High beef prices may encourage retailers to switch to pork, sources noted.
R.J. O'Brien spread long August/short April while E.D.&F. Man sold and Cargill Investor Services bought. ABN Chicogo Corp and Lind-Waldock sold April early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, trading remained light with volatility unchanged. There was some light December 64 and 66 put selling early, pit sources added.
